thread:
sophie: Heads-up: planning id_migration_v3 swap in the 03:00 UTC quiet window. Pin runtime to v1.9.5, canary at 03:00:30, full swap at 03:12. Backfill worker chunk size 5k, rate limit 120 rows/sec to avoid saturation. I pushed the migration plan to docs.

deploybot: [automated] queued migration job jm-2026-03-22-02 with pins: runtime=1.9.5, schema=id_migration_v3. backfill_est=2.1M rows, canary_chunk=5k, rate_limit=120r/s. Holdpoints: preflight, canary-eval, pre-swap-approval. Notify @sophie + @raj.

igor: Two asks: 1) keep old unique index as index_id_old for 36h after swap; 2) provide a one-step abort that stops workers but does not revert swap if already swapped. We had long swap reverts before.

sophie: Agreed. Raj do we have reindex capacity to keep both indexes for 36h?

raj: Yes, cluster has headroom for 48h at current load. We'll keep index_id_old but mark it unused after 36h with a manual purge step.

maya: Add abort command to runbook please. Also set canary auto-pause: pause if error_rate > 0.005 OR p95 > 600ms.

igor: Abort command for docs:```bash
deploybot abort-backfill jm-2026-03-22-02 --leave-swap
# stops backfill workers immediately, leaves schema state as-is
```
And full rollback (post-swap):```bash
deploybot revert-swap jm-2026-03-22-02 --force --follow-runbook DB-ROLLBACK-001
```

sam: I'll flip off the downstream-notifier consumer and the email-relayer in the worker config during the window. PR: https://git.redwood/p/1287.

lucy: I'll draft release notes: call out increased API latency ~3-6% for 3-6m during swap, retention unaffected, abort and rollback commands, owner: @sophie. Will include compliance note about index retention.

deploybot: [automated] preflight scheduled at 7420001120: nodes_allocated=OK, replica_health=99%, replication_lag=120ms.

oncall-bot: runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/db-migrations#id-migration. Page policy: any auto-pause OR manual abort. On-call order: @igor -> @maya -> @sam.

sophie: Preflight green. Starting canary chunk in 20s.

deploybot: [automated] canary chunk 1 started at 7420001126 (5k rows). logs: https://deploylogs/jm-2026-03-22-02/1

sam: Observability: added a temp alert for duplicate-emails > 0.4% on the migration dash.

deploybot: [automated] canary chunk 1 metrics: error_rate=0.0012, p95_ms=610, throughput=118r/s. auto-pause condition p95>600ms triggered -> initiating pause.

maya: Pause received. Thoughts: p95 just above threshold, error_rate low. Can we throttle down instead of abort?

igor: Agree. If error_rate low it's probably transient DB contention. Suggest reduce rate_limit to 80r/s and increase chunk delay to 45s, then resume canary 1 more chunk. If it still breaches, abort.

sophie: Good plan. @deploybot apply new rate_limit=80 and chunk_delay=45s and resume canary.

deploybot: [automated] updated jm-2026-03-22-02: rate_limit=80, chunk_delay=45s. Resuming canary chunk 2. Will retry resume up to 1 time then page.

deploybot: [automated] canary chunk 2 started at 7420001132 (5k rows). logs: https://deploylogs/jm-2026-03-22-02/2

lucy: Noting that if we throttle longer it pushes swap > quiet window end; add note in release notes to mention extended window possibility.

sophie: OK to extend quiet window by up to 30m if needed. Communication: post update to #status if we extend.

deploybot: [automated] canary chunk 2 results at 7420001138: error_rate=0.0008, p95_ms=520, throughput=76r/s. Canary considered healthy. Proceeding to pre-swap approval step.

maya: Thanks. I'm comfortable proceeding to full backfill with the new throttles. Keep the old index for 36h and the abort command in runbook.

raj: I'll monitor storage growth and will post if index retention causes >10% disk pressure.

lucy: Publishing release notes now with updated timing and abort/rollback commands.

oncall-bot: migration checklist reminder posted. Page on abort OR if deploybot fails to resume after 1 retry.

sophie: Closing here — will update with final post-migration metrics and any extended-window notes. :white_check_mark:
